habitat: Fairly secretive pairs in dense bush, usually in the lower stratum.
summary: A common endemic resident. Black above with a white wing-bar. The white throat grades to a cinnamon belly and vent; the cinnamon is always richer towards the belly and vent, and sometimes washes the throat. Southeastern females are dark brown above, not black. The pair duets: ko-ko answered by kweet, boo-boo answered by whee-oo, or phooweeol answered by hueee or churrr, with many variations. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Tropical Boubou has the whole underparts lightly washed pinkish, with less cinnamon on the flanks and vent. Some calls cannot be told apart.
Crimson-breasted Shrike is scarlet below, not white grading to cinnamon.

head.pattern: Black above. White throat, which may carry a pale cinnamon wash.

upperparts.pattern: Black above. The white wing-bar looks narrow or wide depending on how the feathers sit.

underparts.pattern: White throat grades to a cinnamon belly and vent, always richer towards the belly and vent.

wings.pattern: White wing-bar, narrow or wide depending on feather arrangement.

upperparts.pattern: Southeastern females are dark brown above, not black.

underparts.pattern: The cinnamon underparts are described for the species. This variant records only the dark brown upperparts of southeastern females.

calls.description: A duet. ko-ko answered by kweet, or boo-boo answered by whee-oo, or a liquid phooweeol answered by hueee or churrr. Many variations. Grade A recording of two birds calling near Plettenberg Bay, Western Cape. The filename is XC331290-KLCP1.mp3 and does not name the bird.
